findings.rationale: Subgroup screen (Sex) shows FL's Sex=1.0 group has observed/expected ratio 0.10 (outcome rate 0.016 vs mean predicted 0.160), an outlier at z=-7.4 (z_noise -7.3), while the rest of the federation sits near O/E 1. This is the signature of positives in one subgroup being recorded as negatives. The same client also has the largest-magnitude calibration-in-the-large shortfall (CITL +0.072, prevalence 0.079 vs predicted 0.151, z=+4.8) and anomalous updates (median norm ratio 4.17, z=+7.8; mean cosine ~0.005 vs federation ~0.6). Those update anomalies are consistent with training on wrong labels rather than with poisoning, since the local performance is anomalous. Round-1 CITL was already +0.25, so the fault appears to be present from the start.

NJ's Sex=1.0 group has observed/expected ratio 0.10 (outcome rate 0.012 vs mean predicted 0.122), z=-7.4 (z_noise -7.1), again the only subgroup outlier for this client and pointing to under-recorded positives in one subgroup. Overall prevalence is low relative to predicted risk (CITL +0.050, z=+3.3), and its updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 3.01, z=+6.8; mean cosine 0.02 vs federation ~0.6). Local AUC is normal (0.82), which argues against label noise and for a subgroup-specific labeling fault. Round-1 CITL was +0.16, which suggests the fault is present from the start.

SC's Sex=1.0 group has observed/expected ratio 0.16 (outcome rate 0.023 vs mean predicted 0.143), z=-6.9 (z_noise -6.7), consistent with positives in that subgroup being recorded as negatives. Overall CITL is +0.052 (z=+3.4) with prevalence 0.0995 against predicted 0.152. Updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 3.61, z=+7.7; mean cosine -0.065, z=-3.8). Local AUC is 0.79. The SC Sex=0 group is not flagged, so the bias is subgroup-specific. Round-1 CITL was +0.39, which suggests the fault is present from the start.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income). Three clients (FL, NJ, SC) stand out consistently. Each has a Sex=1.0 subgroup with observed/expected ratio near 0.1-0.16 (z about -7), a positive CITL (under-predicted low prevalence), and anomalous update norms (ratio 3-4x median) with near-zero or negative cosine. Their local AUCs are normal-ish, which points to subgroup-specific under-recording of positives rather than poisoning or global label noise. I report them as subgroup_bias with onset round 1, with moderate confidence on the onset round because per-round estimates are noisy. Other single-statistic leads (CT GenHlth p99 z_noise 6.1, DC drift z 3.9, GU norm z 3.9, WV MentHlth p99, AL BMI) were not confirmed by a second independent tool, mostly come from small clients, and were not reported. Budget spent: 20.0 of 20.0.
